TL;DR

Welcome back to Dev Opportunity Radar! 💙

This is a weekly series where I share opportunities, resources, communities, and interesting finds that I come across, with the goal of helping people discover things they might otherwise miss.

This week's edition features Claude Corps 2027 – Third Cohort, a one-year fellowship by Anthropic and CodePath for early-career technologists working with nonprofits and public-interest organizations; a16z FDE Fellowship - Second Cohort, an eight-week program for Forward Deployed Engineers and Applied AI leaders; and Reddit's Game of the Day Hackathon, a virtual hackathon with a $35,000 prize pool.

I'm also sharing Stanford CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents, a graduate course covering everything from agent fundamentals and RAG to tool use, multi-agent systems, memory, and evaluation.

In this edition's 🌟 Community Finds, you'll find three opportunities shared by La Shara Cordero (@earlgreyhot1701d): AI Lab, a free AI career training program from Fair Chance Futures, Columbia University, and USC; the EDSAFE AI Fellowships, focused on the responsible use of AI in education; and the CAIDP AI Policy Clinic, a free program exploring AI policy and governance. Thank you, La Shara, for sharing these with the community!

As always, I'd love to hear from anyone who has discovered something through the Radar. Whether you've applied to an opportunity, attended an event, joined a community, completed a program, or found a useful resource, feel free to share your experience in the comments. With your permission, I'd be happy to feature it in a future 💙 Reader Updates section.

If you've come across an opportunity, resource, community, program, or event that you think others should know about, you're welcome to share that too. I'll always make sure to credit you if I feature it in a future 🌟 Community Finds.

📍 This Week's Opportunities

Here are a few opportunities I came across this week that I thought were worth sharing.

📌 Claude Corps 2027 – Third Cohort

Who it's for: Early-career developers and technologists with hands-on building experience and a background in community, nonprofit, or public-interest work.

What it's about:

Claude Corps is a partnership between Anthropic and CodePath that places fellows inside nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations for one year.

The idea is to work closely with an organization, understand the problems they're facing, and build solutions using Claude. This could mean creating agents, automations, internal tools, dashboards, or integrations. Fellows also help people at the organization learn how to use AI and make sure the solutions can continue working after the fellowship ends.

I found this interesting because it brings together two things: building with AI and using those skills to work on problems that matter to communities. It's also designed for people at the beginning of their careers, rather than requiring several years of professional experience.

Duration: 1 year, starting late August 2027

Format: Full-time, in-person placement in the US

Salary: $85,000 + benefits

Application deadline: January 31, 2027 (applications reviewed on a rolling basis)

A few things to check before applying:

Applicants must complete Anthropic's AI Fluency and Claude 101 courses, have built something (a project, app, automation, or similar), and have experience with a nonprofit, community, or public-interest organization through work, volunteering, or other contributions.

You must also be authorized to work in the US. Visa sponsorship is not available, and fellows should be open to relocating within the country.

Explore Claude Corps and Apply

📌 a16z FDE Fellowship – Second Cohort

Who it's for: Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) and Applied AI leaders.

What it's about:

a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) has opened applications for the second cohort of its FDE Fellowship, an eight-week program starting in January 2027.

For anyone unfamiliar with the term, Forward Deployed Engineers work closely with customers to build and deploy software that fits their specific needs. With more companies adopting AI, this role is becoming an interesting part of how AI products are put into practice.

The fellowship brings together FDEs and Applied AI leaders from different companies. The founding fellows include people from SpaceXSI, OpenAI, Harvey, Exa, Perplexity, Decagon, Cognition, Anthropic, and Replit.

The program runs for eight weeks, with dinners and events every other week. Most events will take place in San Francisco and New York, but fellows can be based anywhere.

Duration: 8 weeks

Starting: Mid-January 2027

Format: Dinners and events every other week

Location: Mostly San Francisco and New York; fellows can be based anywhere

Application deadline: December 31, 2026

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the number of spots is limited.

One thing to note is that this isn't an introductory AI fellowship. It's intended for people already working as FDEs or leading Applied AI teams. I thought it was worth sharing because FDE is a role that more developers might come across as AI adoption grows, and this gives a glimpse into the people and teams working in that space.

If this sounds relevant to your current work, you can check out the details below.

Explore the a16z FDE Fellowship and Apply

📌 Reddit's Game of the Day Hackathon

Who it's for: Developers and game creators interested in building daily games for Reddit.

What it's about:

Reddit is hosting a virtual hackathon where developers can build a new daily game for Reddit using its Developer Platform, Devvit. The idea is to create bite-sized games that give people a reason to come back and play every day. Think daily puzzles, challenges, maps, or other creative game ideas. You can use web technologies like React, Phaser, and Three.js, or game engines such as Unity, Godot, and GameMaker.

There are also some things Reddit is looking for beyond just the gameplay, including a good user experience, fresh ideas, and ways to bring communities together through features like comments, streaks, and daily challenges.

Duration: November 11 – December 8, 2026

Format: Online

Prize pool: $35,000

Application deadline: December 9, 2026, at 7:30 AM IST

A small but important detail: your game must be built using Devvit and run on Reddit to qualify. You don't need to publish it publicly to participate. The hackathon also has a separate category for existing games that developers own and want to bring to Reddit.

I thought this was a fun one to include because it gives developers an opportunity to experiment with game development and build something for an existing platform, rather than starting from scratch with an audience of their own.

Explore the Hackathon and Register

📚 Resources Worth Checking Out

Not every useful find comes with an application deadline.

Here's one resource worth checking out this week.

Stanford CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents

If you've been exploring AI agents and want to understand how to build them beyond basic LLM applications, here's a course worth checking out.

CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents is a Stanford graduate course taught by Professor Diyi Yang, along with PhD students Michael Ryan and John Yang.

The course covers the engineering side of building AI agents, starting with simple LLM pipelines and moving towards compound AI systems and autonomous agents.

Some of the topics covered include:

  • Understanding AI agents and how they differ from workflows
  • Context engineering, RAG, and agentic RAG
  • Tool use, function calling, and MCP
  • Agent frameworks like DSPy and LangGraph
  • Agent design patterns such as ReAct and CodeAct
  • Agent memory and multi-agent systems
  • Prompt optimization, fine-tuning, and evaluation
  • Benchmarks, training data, and agent safety

The lecture series is being released gradually, and 10 lectures are already available, covering topics from agent fundamentals and RAG to multi-agent systems, agent memory, and evaluation. There are also guest lectures, including one featuring the creators of Terminal-Bench.

I thought this was a useful resource for anyone looking to understand the engineering decisions behind building AI agents. You can follow the course schedule to see what's coming next or start watching the available lectures.

Course website | YouTube playlist

🌟 Community Finds

One of my favorite things about this series has been seeing people share opportunities, communities, and resources that others might not have discovered otherwise. It's always nice when something makes its way to the Radar because someone in the community thought others would find it useful.

This time, La Shara Cordero (@earlgreyhot1701d) shared three opportunities that I wanted to bring to your attention. Here they are!

AI Lab – Free AI Career Training

The first one is AI Lab, a free career training program by Fair Chance Futures in partnership with Columbia University and the University of Southern California.

The program is designed for people interested in building careers in the AI economy. Rather than focusing only on learning AI tools, fellows work on real business problems, learn about automation, and develop skills like problem-solving, communication, and collaboration.

It also includes mentorship from MBA students, executive career coaching, interview practice, and certificates from Columbia University and USC.

Duration: February – June 2027, including the career accelerator

Format: Fully remote, with evening classes Monday–Thursday, 6–9 PM local time, and occasional weekend labs

Cost: Free

Application deadline: December 15, 2026

Who can apply: Applicants must be at least 18, have a high school diploma or GED, and have at least two years of work or college experience. They must also live in the Greater New York City or Greater Los Angeles area and be able to commit around 30 hours per week. A laptop can be provided if admitted.

One thing to keep in mind is the time commitment, as this is more than a few hours of online learning each week.

I know this opportunity is location-specific, but I still wanted to include it because of the value it offers. Free AI training, hands-on experience with real business problems, university certificates, and career support together make it worth knowing about, especially for readers who happen to be in those areas.

🔗 Explore AI Lab and Apply

EDSAFE AI Fellowships

Next is the EDSAFE AI Fellowships, a 12-month leadership development program focused on the responsible use of AI in education.

The program brings together people working across education and technology through interactive virtual workshops with experts, mentorship from previous fellows, and a cohort of 30+ members. Fellows also work on a micro-capstone project, applying what they learn to a real-world context.

There are three fellowship tracks:

  • Catalyst Fellowship: For education leaders across practice and industry, including administrators, teachers, researchers, and policymakers interested in AI in education.
  • Women in AI Fellowship: For women working in technology, AI, or data science, as well as women education leaders.
  • Vanguard Fellowship: For people working in K-12 education, including teachers, administrators, IT professionals, and education agency leaders.

Duration: 12 months, starting January 2027

Format: Virtual workshops, cohort discussions, mentorship, and a micro-capstone project

Time commitment: Around 2–4 hours per month

Cost: Fully funded

Application deadline: November 30, 2026, at 10 PM EST

Catalyst and Women in AI are open to applicants worldwide. Vanguard is also open to eligible applicants, but preference is given to those based in the US. Self-nominations are welcome, and fellows will be announced in January 2027. There is no honorarium or compensation.

I wanted to include this because AI in education is a space that needs perspectives from both technology and education. This is also a way to learn from experts, connect with people working in the field, and explore how AI can be used safely and responsibly without requiring a full-time commitment.

🔗 Explore the EDSAFE AI Fellowships and Apply

CAIDP AI Policy Clinic – Spring 2027

The third find is the AI Policy Clinic by the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP). It's a free, semester-long program for people interested in understanding how AI policy is developed and how it affects areas like human rights and democratic values.

The clinic covers topics such as AI history, policy and regulatory frameworks, research methods, and the evaluation of AI policies. It also explores major frameworks and regulations, including the OECD AI Principles, EU AI Act, UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, and the Council of Europe AI Convention.

Participants attend virtual sessions, work on weekly assignments, and collaborate on policy research. Those who successfully complete the requirements receive a CAIDP AI Policy Certificate.

Duration: January 25 – April 16, 2027

Format: Online, with weekly Monday lectures and Friday small-group discussions

Time commitment: Around 6 hours per week

Cost: Free

Application deadline: November 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET

The clinic welcomes applicants from around the world and people from different educational and professional backgrounds. You don't need to be an AI expert to apply. The application includes 23 questions, a short statement explaining your interest (100–200 words), your CV, and one reference.

I wanted to share this because AI policy is an area developers and people from other backgrounds may not have explored yet. If you're curious about how AI regulation, governance, and responsible AI practices work beyond the technical side, this is an opportunity to learn about the field and contribute to policy research.

🔗 Explore the CAIDP AI Policy Clinic and Apply

If you've come across an opportunity, fellowship, grant, hackathon, conference, community, resource, or anything else you think more people should know about, feel free to share it in the comments.

If I feature it in a future edition, I'll always make sure to credit you. If you discovered it, that recognition belongs to you.

One small request: If you're sharing an opportunity, please avoid posting raw URLs directly in the comments. DEV sometimes filters them before I get a chance to see them.

A short description alongside the link makes it much easier for me to review and potentially feature it in a future edition.

💙 Reader Updates

I'm looking forward to this section gradually growing over time, and I'd still love to hear from you.

One of my favorite parts of writing Dev Opportunity Radar has been hearing from people who discovered something they otherwise might have missed.

If you discovered an opportunity through the radar, applied to something, joined a community, attended an event, or simply found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd genuinely love to hear about it.

You don't need to have been accepted or have a big success story to share. Sometimes simply discovering the right opportunity at the right time is already a win.

If you'd like to share an update, feel free to leave a comment on this edition. With your permission, I may feature it in a future 💙 Reader Updates section and tag you so other readers can celebrate your journey too.

I hope this section gradually becomes a place where we can celebrate those stories together, one update at a time.

👋 Until Next Friday

Before I go, I just want to say thank you.

Every week, I spend time searching for opportunities, resources, and communities that I think deserve a little more attention. But one of my favorite parts of this series isn't the research. It's seeing what happens after an edition is published.

Seeing someone discover an opportunity, apply to a program, share a resource, suggest a Community Find, or come back to tell us what they learned reminds me why I started Dev Opportunity Radar in the first place.

The goal has always been simple:

Help people discover opportunities they otherwise might have missed.

Thanks to all of you, it feels like we're doing exactly that.

Whether you've been reading since the very first edition or this is your first time here, thank you for being part of the journey. Every comment, suggestion, and shared opportunity helps make this series better than I could build on my own.

If you ever come across an opportunity, resource, event, community, or anything else you think deserves more attention, I'd love for you to share it in the comments. And if Dev Opportunity Radar helped you discover something exciting, I'd love to hear that too.

Thank you for reading, for sharing, and for helping make this our radar, not just mine.

I'll be back next Friday with more opportunities, resources, and Community Finds.

Until then, take care, and I hope you discover something amazing this week 💙

Free AI training, hands-on experience with real business problems, university certificates, and career support together make it worth knowing about, especially for readers who happen to be in those areas. 🔗 Explore AI Lab and Apply EDSAFE AI Fellowships Next is the EDSAFE AI Fellowships, a 12-month leadership development program focused on the responsible use of AI in education. The program brings together people working across education and technology through interactive virtual workshops with experts, mentorship from previous fellows, and a cohort of 30+ members. Fellows also work on a micro-capstone project, applying what they learn to a real-world context. There are three fellowship tracks: Catalyst Fellowship: For education leaders across practice and industry, including administrators, teachers, researchers, and policymakers interested in AI in education. Women in AI Fellowship: For women working in technology, AI, or data science, as well as women education leaders. Vanguard Fellowship: For people working in K-12 education, including teachers, administrators, IT professionals, and education agency leaders. Duration: 12 months, starting January 2027 Format: Virtual workshops, cohort discussions, mentorship, and a micro-capstone project Time commitment: Around 2–4 hours per month Cost: Fully funded Application deadline: November 30, 2026, at 10 PM EST Catalyst and Women in AI are open to applicants worldwide. Vanguard is also open to eligible applicants, but preference is given to those based in the US. Self-nominations are welcome, and fellows will be announced in January 2027. There is no honorarium or compensation. I wanted to include this because AI in education is a space that needs perspectives from both technology and education. This is also a way to learn from experts, connect with people working in the field, and explore how AI can be used safely and responsibly without requiring a full-time commitment. 🔗 Explore the EDSAFE AI Fellowships and Apply CAIDP AI Policy Clinic – Spring 2027 The third find is the AI Policy Clinic by the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP). It's a free, semester-long program for people interested in understanding how AI policy is developed and how it affects areas like human rights and democratic values. The clinic covers topics such as AI history, policy and regulatory frameworks, research methods, and the evaluation of AI policies. It also explores major frameworks and regulations, including the OECD AI Principles, EU AI Act, UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, and the Council of Europe AI Convention. Participants attend virtual sessions, work on weekly assignments, and collaborate on policy research. Those who successfully complete the requirements receive a CAIDP AI Policy Certificate. Duration: January 25 – April 16, 2027 Format: Online, with weekly Monday lectures and Friday small-group discussions Time commitment: Around 6 hours per week Cost: Free Application deadline: November 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET The clinic welcomes applicants from around the world and people from different educational and professional backgrounds. You don't need to be an AI expert to apply. The application includes 23 questions, a short statement explaining your interest (100–200 words), your CV, and one reference. I wanted to share this because AI policy is an area developers and people from other backgrounds may not have explored yet. If you're curious about how AI regulation, governance, and responsible AI practices work beyond the technical side, this is an opportunity to learn about the field and contribute to policy research. 🔗 Explore the CAIDP AI Policy Clinic and Apply A big thank you to La Shara Cordero (@earlgreyhot1701d) for thinking of the Radar and sharing these with the community. And thank you to everyone who takes the time to send something my way. It really does mean a lot 💙 I'd love for this section to keep growing. If you've come across an opportunity, fellowship, grant, hackathon, conference, community, resource, or anything else you think more people should know about, feel free to share it in the comments. If I feature it in a future edition, I'll always make sure to credit you. If you discovered it, that recognition belongs to you. One small request: If you're sharing an opportunity, please avoid posting raw URLs directly in the comments. DEV sometimes filters them before I get a chance to see them. A short description alongside the link makes it much easier for me to review and potentially feature it in a future edition. 💙 Reader Updates I'm looking forward to this section gradually growing over time, and I'd still love to hear from you. One of my favorite parts of writing Dev Opportunity Radar has been hearing from people who discovered something they otherwise might have missed. If you discovered an opportunity through the radar, applied to something, joined a community, attended an event, or simply found a resource you hadn't seen before, I'd genuinely love to hear about it. You don't need to have been accepted or have a big success story to share. Sometimes simply discovering the right opportunity at the right time is already a win. If you'd like to share an update, feel free to leave a comment on this edition. With your permission, I may feature it in a future 💙 Reader Updates section and tag you so other readers can celebrate your journey too. I hope this section gradually becomes a place where we can celebrate those stories together, one update at a time. 👋 Until Next Friday Before I go, I just want to say thank you. Every week, I spend time searching for opportunities, resources, and communities that I think deserve a little more attention. But one of my favorite parts of this series isn't the research. It's seeing what happens after an edition is published. Seeing someone discover an opportunity, apply to a program, share a resource, suggest a Community Find, or come back to tell us what they learned reminds me why I started Dev Opportunity Radar in the first place. The goal has always been simple: Help people discover opportunities they otherwise might have missed. Thanks to all of you, it feels like we're doing exactly that. Whether you've been reading since the very first edition or this is your first time here, thank you for being part of the journey. Every comment, suggestion, and shared opportunity helps make this series better than I could build on my own. If you ever come across an opportunity, resource, event, community, or anything else you think deserves more attention, I'd love for you to share it in the comments. And if Dev Opportunity Radar helped you discover something exciting, I'd love to hear that too. Thank you for reading, for sharing, and for helping make this our radar, not just mine. I'll be back next Friday with more opportunities, resources, and Community Finds. content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Welcome back to Dev Opportunity Radar! 💙 This is a weekly series where I share opportunities, resources, communities, and interesting finds that I come across, with the goal of helping people discover things they might otherwise miss. This week's edition features Claude Corps 2027 – Third Cohort, a one-year fellowship by Anthropic and CodePath for early-career technologists working with nonprofits and public-interest organizations; a16z FDE Fellowship - Second Cohort, an eight-week program for Forward Deployed Engineers and Applied AI leaders; and Reddit's Game of the Day Hackathon, a virtual hackathon with a $35,000 prize pool. I'm also sharing Stanford CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents, a graduate course covering everything from agent fundamentals and RAG to tool use, multi-agent systems, memory, and evaluation. In this edition's 🌟 Community Finds, you'll find three opportunities shared by La Shara Cordero (@earlgreyhot1701d): AI Lab, a free AI career training program from Fair Chance Futures, Columbia University, and USC; the EDSAFE AI Fellowships, focused on the responsible use of AI in education; and the CAIDP AI Policy Clinic, a free program exploring AI policy and governance. Thank you, La Shara, for sharing these with the community! As always, I'd love to hear from anyone who has discovered something through the Radar. 📌 Claude Corps 2027 – Third Cohort

Who it's for: Early-career developers and technologists with hands-on building experience and a background in community, nonprofit, or public-interest work.

What it's about:

Claude Corps is a partnership between Anthropic and CodePath that places fellows inside nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations for one year.

The idea is to work closely with an organization, understand the problems they're facing, and build solutions using Claude. This could mean creating agents, automations, internal tools, dashboards, or integrations. Fellows also help people at the organization learn how to use AI and make sure the solutions can continue working after the fellowship ends.

I found this interesting because it brings together two things: building with AI and using those skills to work on problems that matter to communities. It's also designed for people at the beginning of their careers, rather than requiring several years of professional experience.

Duration: 1 year, starting late August 2027

Format: Full-time, in-person placement in the US

Salary: $85,000 + benefits

Application deadline: January 31, 2027 (applications reviewed on a rolling basis)

A few things to check before applying:

Applicants must complete Anthropic's AI Fluency and Claude 101 courses, have built something (a project, app, automation, or similar), and have experience with a nonprofit, community, or public-interest organization through work, volunteering, or other contributions.

You must also be authorized to work in the US. Visa sponsorship is not available, and fellows should be open to relocating within the country.

📌 a16z FDE Fellowship – Second Cohort

Who it's for: Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) and Applied AI leaders.

What it's about:

a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) has opened applications for the second cohort of its FDE Fellowship, an eight-week program starting in January 2027.

For anyone unfamiliar with the term, Forward Deployed Engineers work closely with customers to build and deploy software that fits their specific needs. With more companies adopting AI, this role is becoming an interesting part of how AI products are put into practice.

The fellowship brings together FDEs and Applied AI leaders from different companies. The founding fellows include people from SpaceXSI, OpenAI, Harvey, Exa, Perplexity, Decagon, Cognition, Anthropic, and Replit.

The program runs for eight weeks, with dinners and events every other week. Most events will take place in San Francisco and New York, but fellows can be based anywhere.

Duration: 8 weeks

Starting: Mid-January 2027

Format: Dinners and events every other week

Location: Mostly San Francisco and New York; fellows can be based anywhere

Application deadline: December 31, 2026

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the number of spots is limited.

One thing to note is that this isn't an introductory AI fellowship. It's intended for people already working as FDEs or leading Applied AI teams. I thought it was worth sharing because FDE is a role that more developers might come across as AI adoption grows, and this gives a glimpse into the people and teams working in that space.

📌 Reddit's Game of the Day Hackathon

Who it's for: Developers and game creators interested in building daily games for Reddit.

What it's about:

Reddit is hosting a virtual hackathon where developers can build a new daily game for Reddit using its Developer Platform, Devvit. The idea is to create bite-sized games that give people a reason to come back and play every day. Think daily puzzles, challenges, maps, or other creative game ideas. You can use web technologies like React, Phaser, and Three.js, or game engines such as Unity, Godot, and GameMaker.

There are also some things Reddit is looking for beyond just the gameplay, including a good user experience, fresh ideas, and ways to bring communities together through features like comments, streaks, and daily challenges.

Duration: November 11 – December 8, 2026

Format: Online

Prize pool: $35,000

Application deadline: December 9, 2026, at 7:30 AM IST

A small but important detail: your game must be built using Devvit and run on Reddit to qualify. You don't need to publish it publicly to participate. The hackathon also has a separate category for existing games that developers own and want to bring to Reddit.

I thought this was a fun one to include because it gives developers an opportunity to experiment with game development and build something for an existing platform, rather than starting from scratch with an audience of their own.

Stanford CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents

If you've been exploring AI agents and want to understand how to build them beyond basic LLM applications, here's a course worth checking out.

CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents is a Stanford graduate course taught by Professor Diyi Yang, along with PhD students Michael Ryan and John Yang.

The course covers the engineering side of building AI agents, starting with simple LLM pipelines and moving towards compound AI systems and autonomous agents.

Some of the topics covered include:

  • Understanding AI agents and how they differ from workflows
  • Context engineering, RAG, and agentic RAG
  • Tool use, function calling, and MCP
  • Agent frameworks like DSPy and LangGraph
  • Agent design patterns such as ReAct and CodeAct
  • Agent memory and multi-agent systems
  • Prompt optimization, fine-tuning, and evaluation
  • Benchmarks, training data, and agent safety

The lecture series is being released gradually, and 10 lectures are already available, covering topics from agent fundamentals and RAG to multi-agent systems, agent memory, and evaluation. There are also guest lectures, including one featuring the creators of Terminal-Bench.

I thought this was a useful resource for anyone looking to understand the engineering decisions behind building AI agents. You can follow the course schedule to see what's coming next or start watching the available lectures.

AI Lab – Free AI Career Training

The first one is AI Lab, a free career training program by Fair Chance Futures in partnership with Columbia University and the University of Southern California.

The program is designed for people interested in building careers in the AI economy. Rather than focusing only on learning AI tools, fellows work on real business problems, learn about automation, and develop skills like problem-solving, communication, and collaboration.

It also includes mentorship from MBA students, executive career coaching, interview practice, and certificates from Columbia University and USC.

Duration: February – June 2027, including the career accelerator

Format: Fully remote, with evening classes Monday–Thursday, 6–9 PM local time, and occasional weekend labs

费用：免费

Application deadline: December 15, 2026

Who can apply: Applicants must be at least 18, have a high school diploma or GED, and have at least two years of work or college experience. They must also live in the Greater New York City or Greater Los Angeles area and be able to commit around 30 hours per week. A laptop can be provided if admitted.

One thing to keep in mind is the time commitment, as this is more than a few hours of online learning each week.

I know this opportunity is location-specific, but I still wanted to include it because of the value it offers. Free AI training, hands-on experience with real business problems, university certificates, and career support together make it worth knowing about, especially for readers who happen to be in those areas.

EDSAFE AI Fellowships

Next is the EDSAFE AI Fellowships, a 12-month leadership development program focused on the responsible use of AI in education.

The program brings together people working across education and technology through interactive virtual workshops with experts, mentorship from previous fellows, and a cohort of 30+ members. Fellows also work on a micro-capstone project, applying what they learn to a real-world context.

There are three fellowship tracks:

  • Catalyst Fellowship: For education leaders across practice and industry, including administrators, teachers, researchers, and policymakers interested in AI in education.
  • Women in AI Fellowship: For women working in technology, AI, or data science, as well as women education leaders.
  • Vanguard Fellowship: For people working in K-12 education, including teachers, administrators, IT professionals, and education agency leaders.

Duration: 12 months, starting January 2027

Format: Virtual workshops, cohort discussions, mentorship, and a micro-capstone project

Time commitment: Around 2–4 hours per month

Cost: Fully funded

Application deadline: November 30, 2026, at 10 PM EST

Catalyst and Women in AI are open to applicants worldwide. Vanguard is also open to eligible applicants, but preference is given to those based in the US. Self-nominations are welcome, and fellows will be announced in January 2027. There is no honorarium or compensation.

I wanted to include this because AI in education is a space that needs perspectives from both technology and education. This is also a way to learn from experts, connect with people working in the field, and explore how AI can be used safely and responsibly without requiring a full-time commitment.

CAIDP AI Policy Clinic – Spring 2027

The third find is the AI Policy Clinic by the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP). It's a free, semester-long program for people interested in understanding how AI policy is developed and how it affects areas like human rights and democratic values.

The clinic covers topics such as AI history, policy and regulatory frameworks, research methods, and the evaluation of AI policies. It also explores major frameworks and regulations, including the OECD AI Principles, EU AI Act, UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, and the Council of Europe AI Convention.

Participants attend virtual sessions, work on weekly assignments, and collaborate on policy research. Those who successfully complete the requirements receive a CAIDP AI Policy Certificate.

Duration: January 25 – April 16, 2027

Format: Online, with weekly Monday lectures and Friday small-group discussions

Time commitment: Around 6 hours per week

费用：免费

Application deadline: November 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET

The clinic welcomes applicants from around the world and people from different educational and professional backgrounds. You don't need to be an AI expert to apply. The application includes 23 questions, a short statement explaining your interest (100–200 words), your CV, and one reference.

I wanted to share this because AI policy is an area developers and people from other backgrounds may not have explored yet. If you're curious about how AI regulation, governance, and responsible AI practices work beyond the technical side, this is an opportunity to learn about the field and contribute to policy research.
